# Ticker Pack: MICROSOFT CORP (MSFT)

**2026-10-11** · company dossier · insider flow (90d) · 12 institutional holders (sample) · 79 sources

## Executive summary

Microsoft Corp trades on Nasdaq under the ticker MSFT and is registered with the SEC under CIK 0000789019. By its own SEC classification it sits in SIC code "Services-Prepackaged Software" - the agency's label for the company's reported line of business, and the only business categorisation these measured facts establish. The pack's Company section carries the full dossier narrative on the business, its financials and its risk disclosures, built from 3 10-K filings, 3 10-Q filings, 6 8-K filings and 4 grounded web angles, so this summary does not restate that ground.

The recent filing cadence is dominated almost entirely by insider-reporting traffic. Across the 24 most recent submissions on EDGAR, the counted-by-form breakdown is 22 Form 4s, one Form 144 and one PX14A6G. Those 24 filings span a narrow calendar band from 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-17, with clusters of Form 4s filed on 2026-09-11 (ten of them, all for period 2026-09-10) and on 2026-09-17 (five, all for period 2026-09-15). A Form 144 - notice of a proposed sale of restricted securities - was filed on 2026-09-14, and a PX14A6G, an exempt solicitation notice filed by a shareholder rather than by the company, was filed on 2026-09-09. No periodic report (10-K or 10-Q) appears inside this most-recent-24 window, so the window itself says nothing about the timing of the next earnings report; it is a snapshot of compensation-driven and holder-driven paperwork, not of company disclosure.

The insider flow measurement covers 2026-07-13 to 2026-10-11, a 90-day window. In that period there were 43 Form 4 filings, all 43 of which were read, yielding 42 parsed transactions. Direction is one-sided: zero open-market buys, totalling $0 across zero distinct insiders, against 16 open-market sells totalling $71.4M across 4 distinct insiders. Net open-market flow for the window is therefore **-$71.4M**. The remainder of the activity is non-discretionary or compensation-linked rather than directional: 14 awards, 11 tax-withholding dispositions and zero option exercises. Four selling insiders is a narrow base, and the measurement does not attribute amounts to named individuals, so the figure describes aggregate direction in one quarter, not a judgement about any one officer or director.

On 5%-plus ownership, the only disclosure captured between 2025-09-06 and 2026-10-11 is from The Vanguard Group, which reported falling **below 5%** as of 03/13/2026. No other 13G or 13D disclosure appears in that window.

The institutional-holder picture is explicitly partial. EDGAR full-text search matched 8,559 13F-HR information tables naming Microsoft over 2026-05-14 to 2026-10-11; of those, 12 were scanned and all 12 reported a position, together accounting for 14,137,239 shares. Within that sample the largest reported positions by share count are BNP Paribas Financial Markets at 7,319,367 shares (reported value $2.73B, period 2026-06-30); Coatue Management LLC at 5,171,976 shares ($2.50B, period 2025-12-31); Alkeon Capital Management LLC at 851,176 shares ($317.5M, period 2026-06-30); Rokos Capital Management LLP at 279,213 shares ($104.1M, 2026-06-30); Soltis Investment Advisors LLC at 226,152 shares ($84.4M, 2026-06-30); Maplelane Capital, LLC at 157,900 shares ($58.9M, 2026-06-30); Hall Laurie J Trustee at 52,624 shares ($27.0M, 2026-09-30); and ZEGA Investments, LLC at 38,149 shares ($14.2M, 2026-06-30). Reported dollar values are not comparable across filers - some still report in thousands - and must not be summed. This is a sample, not the complete holder list: 12 scanned tables out of 8,559 matches, and the period dates within the sample range from 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30, so the rankings reflect different as-of dates.

## Company

### MICROSOFT CORP (MSFT): COMPANY DUE-DILIGENCE DOSSIER

---

#### 1. SNAPSHOT

Microsoft Corporation (CIK 789019) is a global technology company whose current commercial center of gravity is cloud infrastructure and AI services, delivered through three reporting segments disclosed in its guidance framework: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing [20]. The company reports on a June fiscal year end; its most recent annual report is the 10-K for the period ended June 30, 2026, filed July 29, 2026 [1].

**Live quote:** the live quote shows MSFT last trading at 535.195 USD, with a day range of 526.36-537.19 against a prior close of 522.69. The 52-week range and the day's net change were not supplied in the quote feed, so no statement about longer-term price trend can be grounded here.

**Bottom line.** On the reported figures, Microsoft presents as one of the strongest balance sheets and income statements available in public markets: FY2026 operating income of $155.24B on an asset base of $758.38B, stockholders' equity of $442.39B against total liabilities of $315.99B, and net income of $133.75B. Growth is being driven by cloud and AI - FY2026 revenue of $331.84B, up roughly 18%, with Azure revenue growth of 41% and commercial remaining performance obligations up 84% to $678 billion [15][20]. The counterweights are concentrated and real: an enormous capital-expenditure program ($145.3B committed in FY2026, with FY2027 capex indicated to be held "flat at $190 billion" per one web report) [13], a $28.9B IRS transfer-pricing claim that the company is contesting [19], and ongoing restructuring in the gaming business [16]. This is a trust-and-partner-grade counterparty on financial capacity; the diligence question is not solvency but whether AI-era capital intensity and tax/regulatory tail risk compress the returns that the current income statement implies.

---

#### 2. BUSINESS & RECENT FILINGS

**Annual reports.** The company has filed 10-Ks for FY2024 (filed 2024-07-30), FY2025 (filed 2025-07-30), and FY2026 (filed 2026-07-29), giving a clean three-year comparative baseline for diligence [3][2][1]. The FY2026 10-K was filed the same day as an 8-K dated July 29, 2026 [8], consistent with the earnings release of that date [20].

**Quarterly reports.** Three 10-Qs are on file for fiscal 2026: Q1 (period 2025-09-30, filed 2025-10-29) [6], Q2 (period 2025-12-31, filed 2026-01-28) [5], and Q3 (period 2026-03-31, filed 2026-04-29) [4]. Each quarterly filing was paired with a same-day 8-K - January 28, 2026 [12] and April 29, 2026 [11] - the standard earnings-release cadence.

**Other 8-Ks.** Four additional current reports fall outside the earnings calendar: 8-Ks filed 2026-05-14 (period 2026-05-13) [10], 2026-06-05 (period 2026-06-02) [9], and 2026-09-02 (period 2026-09-02) [7]. The material provided here does not include the content of these three filings, so their subject matter cannot be characterized; a buyer of this dossier should pull them directly as a diligence follow-up.

**What the newest 10-Q's own words disclose.** The Q3 FY2026 10-Q sets out an unusually broad list of critical estimates management must make - standalone selling price of performance obligations, variable consideration, product returns and refunds, loss contingencies, the fair value and potential impairment of goodwill and intangible assets for reporting units, product life cycles, useful lives of tangible and intangible assets, allowances for doubtful accounts, stock-based compensation forfeiture rates, the point at which technological feasibility is achieved, uncertain tax positions, and the timing and amount of investment impairments [4]. For an investment portfolio of Microsoft's scale, the filing is explicit that equity investments not carried at fair value are tested qualitatively for impairment with changes running through other income (expense), net, that equity-method investments may be recorded on a lag of up to three months, and that "[i]f market, industry, and/or investee conditions deteriorate, we may incur future impairments" [4]. Derivative positions are disclosed at $1,080 million of assets and $671 million of liabilities at March 31, 2026, against $758 million and $1,837 million respectively at June 30, 2025 [4].

---

#### 3. FINANCIAL POSTURE

**Income statement (FY2026, per reported XBRL).** Operating income was $155.24B and pre-tax income $165.93B, with income tax expense of $32.19B producing net income of $133.75B; basic EPS was reported at 18. The earnings release puts full-year revenue above $331.8B, up 18%, with full-year operating income of $155.2B, up 21% [20] - consistent with the reported operating income figure. Full-year GAAP EPS is reported in the web research at $17.95, with Q4 revenue of $90.0B (up 18%, 17% in constant currency), Q4 operating income of $40.6B (up 18%), and Q4 GAAP net income of $35.8B at $4.81 diluted EPS [20].

**Operating-to-net bridge.** The $10.69B gap between operating income ($155.24B) and pre-tax income ($165.93B) is accounted for by reported non-operating income of $10.70B - i.e., non-operating items *added* to, rather than subtracted from, pre-tax earnings. The Q3 10-Q shows the composition of that line in detail for the nine months ended March 31, 2026: interest and dividends income of $2,546 million, interest expense of $(2,212) million, net recognized gains on investments of $1,419 million, net gains on derivatives of $1,740 million, net losses on foreign currency remeasurement of $(367) million, and "Other, net" of $4,127 million, totalling $7,253 million versus $(3,194) million in the prior-year nine months - a swing of more than $10 billion in that single line [4]. The filing further states that other income (expense), net included $19 million of net losses for the three months and $5.9 billion of net gains for the nine months ended March 31, 2026, against net losses of $768 million and $2.7 billion in the comparable prior-year periods [4]. Separately, the Q4 release attributes a $0.27 per share benefit to a $3.2 billion gain on an investment in Anthropic, alongside lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program expenses, partially offset by severance and impairment charges in Xbox [20]. **Diligence implication:** a material slice of FY2026's year-over-year net-income acceleration (net income up 31% per [15]) sits in investment and derivative gains, not in operations. Those are real but non-recurring in character.

**Balance sheet.** Total assets of $758.38B against total liabilities of $315.99B leaves $442.39B of stockholders' equity - a liabilities-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.71x. Cash and equivalents were reported at $20.93B, which is the narrow cash line only; the material provided here does not break out short-term investments, so the figure should not be read as total liquidity.

**Data caveat the buyer must know.** The XBRL revenue tags supplied in this material are stale and internally inconsistent with the FY2026 annual filing: they report "latest annual" total revenue of $16.04B (FY2010 10-K filed 2010-07-30) and a most recent quarterly figure of $19.95B (period ending 2010-12-31). These are clearly legacy-period tags, not FY2026 figures, and they conflict with the $331.84B FY2026 revenue in the earnings release and web research [20][15]. All revenue analysis in this dossier therefore relies on the FY2026 press release and web sources, not the XBRL revenue field.

**Capital intensity.** One web report states Microsoft committed $145.3 billion to capital expenses for full fiscal 2026, roughly two-thirds for CPUs and GPUs deployed in clusters and the remaining third for datacenter facilities and other long-lived assets, and that Microsoft would hold fiscal 2027 capex "flat at $190 billion," choosing not to accelerate spending [13]. The $145.3B and "flat at $190 billion" figures are not reconcilable with each other on their face; the material provided here does not explain the basis of either number, and a buyer should verify both against the 10-K cash flow statement [1].

---

#### 4. RECENT DEVELOPMENTS

- **FY2026 results (July 29, 2026).** Microsoft Cloud Q4 revenue of $59.3 billion (up 27%) drove full-year cloud revenue past $214 billion; commercial remaining performance obligations jumped 84% to $678 billion [20][15]. Azure revenue crossed the $100 billion mark during fiscal 2026 per one report [13], with Azure growth of 41% for the year [15].
- **FY2027 guidance.** Q1 FY2027 total revenue was guided to $89.85B - $90.95B (16% - 17% growth), with Intelligent Cloud at $40.95B - $41.25B (33% - 34% growth) and Azure growth of approximately 45% in constant currency; Productivity and Business Processes at $36.7B - $37.0B and More Personal Computing at $12.2B - $12.7B [20]. Guiding Azure *acceleration* into FY2027 is the single most important forward claim in the file.
- **Competitive position.** Per the web research, Azure ranks second in global cloud infrastructure behind AWS and ahead of Google Cloud, with Synergy Research Group putting Azure at 20% - 25% share versus AWS at 28% - 31% and Google Cloud at 12% - 15%; in Europe Azure sits near 27% against AWS at 29%. Microsoft extended its strategic partnership with OpenAI in October 2025 and April 2026, with Azure as OpenAI's exclusive underlying cloud provider, and began scaling its custom Maia 100 AI chip.
- **Gaming restructuring.** Microsoft is eliminating roughly 3,200 Xbox roles across fiscal 2027, with 1,600 cut at the time of the report, and four studios - including Double Fine and Ninja Theory - leaving Xbox, with no publicly announced games cancelled [16].
- **Windows/devices.** At an October 7, 2026 Windows and Surface event, Microsoft's Windows leadership said Copilot+ PCs are shipping in the tens of millions of units a year and account for more than 40% of laptops being built for business, alongside a new "hybrid intelligence" strategy for splitting AI work [14].
- **Immigration/labor.** One market-structure note references a US Labor Department suspension of Microsoft and other companies from the PERM green-card program, describing it as a source of short-term volatility while characterizing overall sentiment as bullish and the stock as above its moving averages [17].

---

#### 5. INSIDER ACTIVITY

Form 4 filings in the window show a dense, date-clustered pattern across both management and the board. **Note: this data is filing metadata only - filer name and filing date. It contains no transaction direction, share count, or price, so no conclusion about insider buying or selling can or should be drawn.**

- **September 11, 2026 (10 filers, predominantly directors):** Emma N. Walmsley, John D. Rainey, Penny S. Pritzker, Sandra E. Peterson, Mark Mason, Catherine MacGregor, Teri List, Hugh F. Johnston, Reid Hoffman, and Carmine Di Sibio.
- **September 15, 2026:** Alice L. Jolla, Amy Coleman, and Amy Hood.
- **September 17, 2026:** Bradford L. Smith, Takeshi Numoto, Amy Hood, Amy Coleman, and Judson Althoff.

The tight clustering of ten board filings on a single date, and of senior officers (CFO Amy Hood appears on two dates) two days later, is the signature of a scheduled, calendar-driven event rather than discretionary activity - but the data supplied does not identify the underlying transaction type, and this dossier makes no claim about it. A buyer wanting direction and size should retrieve the Form 4 documents themselves.

---

#### 6. RISKS & RED FLAGS

1. **IRS transfer-pricing exposure - the largest discrete quantified risk in the file.** On September 26, 2023 Microsoft received Notices of Proposed Adjustment from the IRS for tax years 2004-2013, announced October 11, 2023, with the primary issues relating to intercompany transfer pricing [19]. The web research states the IRS seeks an additional **$28.9 billion plus penalties and interest**, that Microsoft disagrees and will "vigorously contest the NOPAs" through administrative appeals and if necessary judicial proceedings, that unrecognized tax benefits and long-term income tax liabilities stood at $28.7 billion as of December 31, 2025, that tax years 2014-2017 remain under IRS audit, and that Irish operations remain open for 2021 and thereafter. The claim is roughly 6.5% of total equity ($442.39B) - survivable, but not immaterial.
2. **Capital intensity and depreciation drag.** With roughly two-thirds of FY2026's $145.3B capex going to CPUs and GPUs [13], the fixed-cost base being laid down is substantial and short-lived relative to real estate. Management's choice not to accelerate FY2027 spending [13] is prudent, but the useful-lives estimate is explicitly one of the critical judgments in the filings [4].
3. **Earnings quality.** FY2026 net income benefited from large non-operating gains - including a $3.2 billion Anthropic investment gain worth $0.27 per share in Q4 [20] - and the nine-month "Other, net" line swung to $4,127 million of income from $(2,861) million [4]. Operating income growth (21%) is a cleaner read than net income growth (31%) [20][15].
4. **Investment-portfolio impairment risk.** The 10-Q warns directly that deteriorating market, industry or investee conditions "may" cause future impairments, and that equity-method results may lag up to three months [4] - relevant given the scale of AI-adjacent stakes.
5. **Legal and regulatory.** Accrued legal liabilities of $575 million at December 31, 2025 (from $530 million at September 30, 2025), with reasonably possible losses of approximately $400 million beyond accruals, per the web research. The LinkedIn/Irish Data Protection Commission GDPR matter - opened 2018, final decision with a fine in October 2024, appealed November 2024, preliminary hearing December 2025 - remains live [18].
6. **Segment divergence.** Xbox is in active contraction (≈3,200 roles, four studios divested) with severance and impairment charges already recognized [16][20], and More Personal Computing is guided to the lowest growth of the three segments [20].
7. **Source-quality caveat.** Several key figures (market share, Azure run-rate, OpenAI terms, legal accruals) come from secondary web aggregators rather than filings and could not be verified against primary documents in this material.

---

#### 7. DILIGENCE READ

Microsoft reads as a counterparty of exceptional financial capacity whose risk profile has shifted from *business* risk to *capital-allocation* risk. The equity base of $442.39B, liabilities of $315.99B, and FY2026 operating income of $155.24B leave very wide coverage for the quantified tail risks in this file - the $28.9B IRS claim [19] and sub-billion-dollar legal accruals included. Demand signal is the strongest datapoint available: commercial RPO up 84% to $678 billion [20] is a multi-year contracted backlog that underwrites the FY2027 Azure acceleration guidance of ~45% constant-currency growth [20].

Three things would change the read. First, whether operating margin holds as the depreciation from $145.3B of FY2026 capex lands [13] - strip out the investment gains and the operating line, not the net line, is the honest metric. Second, resolution path on the IRS NOPAs, which is contested and unresolved in this material [19]. Third, the contents of the three non-earnings 8-Ks from May, June and September 2026 [10][9][7], which this material does not describe and which a paying buyer should obtain before relying on this dossier as complete. For a partner or vendor-risk decision, the answer is clearly favorable; for an investment decision at 535.195 USD, the file supports the growth thesis but does not contain the valuation inputs (52-week range, multiples, consensus) needed to judge price.

### INSIDER FLOW REPORT: MICROSOFT CORP (MSFT, CIK 0000789019)
##### Form 4 filings, 2026-07-13 through 2026-10-11

---

#### SNAPSHOT

Across the 91-day window, 43 Form 4 filings were fetched and read (all 43 that fell in the window), containing 42 non-derivative transactions, 19 derivative transactions and 35 reported-holdings rows [64].

The flow is one-directional and simple:

- **Open-market purchases: zero.** No insider bought a single MSFT share on the open market in this window - 0 shares, $0, 0 distinct insiders.
- **Open-market sales: 16 transaction lines**, totalling **143,009.353 shares for $71,420,551**, spread across **four insiders** - all of them senior operating executives.
- **Net open-market flow: -$71.4 million.**

Everything else in the file is mechanical compensation plumbing: 14 grant/award lines [A], 11 tax-withholding dispositions [F], one gift [G], and 19 derivative RSU award lines for non-employee directors. Zero option exercises are recorded in the material.

Sales were concentrated in a narrow calendar band: four of the four selling insiders transacted between 2026-08-04 and 2026-09-14, immediately around Microsoft's annual late-August equity vest/grant cycle.

**None.** The material contains no [P] transactions by any officer, director or 10% holder in this window. There is no buy cluster, and no lone buyer, to interpret.

#### SIGNAL READ

The honest read is that this window contains **no conviction signal in either direction** - and specifically, nothing that should be read as a bearish tell.

The headline, -$71.4m of net open-market flow with zero buys, looks severe in isolation. Three things temper it:

1. **The selling is tightly coupled to the compensation calendar.** Nadella's 86,525-share sale landed the day after a 178,622-share award and a 70,466-share tax surrender [55][52]; Hood's 41,674-share sale sat one day before a 29,077-share award [28][23]. Executives whose pay is overwhelmingly stock routinely monetise a slice of a vest to diversify and to fund the cash side of a tax bill. Nothing in the material distinguishes this from that ordinary pattern.
2. **Post-sale positions remain very large.** Nadella still reports 572,247.534 shares directly plus roughly 431,000 shares across five GRATs [52]; Hood 562,701.427 [23]; Althoff 141,167.886 [25]; Numoto 59,412.24 [22]. No one sold out.
3. **Multi-tranche, single-day execution** across eight (Nadella) and six (Hood) price prints is characteristic of a worked or pre-scheduled order rather than an opportunistic exit [52][28].

The stronger insider signal - **clustered open-market buying** - is entirely absent here, but so is its opposite: there is no broadening of sellers, no director selling, and no sale by Smith, Coleman or Jolla despite all three vesting equity in the same cycle.

**Caveats, stated plainly.** Form 4 covers only officers, directors and 10% holders, and is filed within two business days of the trade, so this is a narrow and lagging lens. A Form 4 discloses *what* happened, never *why* - it carries no statement of intent, and sales may be driven by taxes, diversification, trusts, philanthropy or a pre-set plan. The material summarised here does not include footnote text identifying 10b5-1 plans, so no such designation is claimed; plans may nonetheless be in place. Any gap in this file is a limit of the material, not a finding about Microsoft or any individual. **This is not investment advice.**
